Josh Hartnett, Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson sat down with Amazon for a rapid-fire Q&A game, where they shared thoughts on what makes a good book. As Hathaway explains, “Since ‘Verity’ is all about finishing a story, today we’re finishing a few sentences about the kinds of books we can’t put down.”

articles.title: Jerry Golod, Producer of ‘Tales From the Darkside’ and Former CBS And NBC Executive, Dies at 87
articles.summary: Jerry Golod, the producer of “Tales From the Darkside,” died following a brief battle with cancer at his home in Rancho Mirage, Calif., on Wednesday. He was 87. Throughout his career, Golod served as an executive at CBS and NBC, later launching JayGee Productions in the early 1980s.
body: In 1975, Golod became vice president of children’s programs at CBS before moving to NBC Entertainment in 1979 as vice president and national program director. While there, he oversaw daytime and children’s programming, specials, variety and West Coast late-night programming. He later joined CBS Television Studios and The CW in developing a new revival of “Tales From the Darkside,” though the series never moved past a 2015 pilot.

Golod executive produced CBS’s “Brass” in 1985 and “Return to Green Acres,” which reunited cast members of the 1960s sitcom. He also executive produced the 1991 revival of “Land of the Lost,” which ran for two seasons.

Golod was born in the Bronx on Dec. 26, 1938, and graduated from City College of New York. He began his career at advertising agency Dancer Fitzgerald Sample and went on to become vice president and associate director of programming. He also spent three years overseeing a television production company affiliated with the agency.
In the ‘90s, Golod worked with Pet Television Network as co-chairman and co-owner of a cable and satellite service aimed toward animal enthusiasts.

articles.title: Asghar Farhadi Says Films Like ‘Argo’ Perpetuate American White Savior Myth: ‘Who Asked You To Come and Save Us?’
articles.summary: RIO DE JANEIRO, Brazil – Twice Oscar-winning filmmaker Asghar Farhadi, who is at the Rio Film Festival to present “Parallel Tales,” spoke about the perceived hegemony of American cinema and how Hollywood shouldn’t be seen as a source for faithful portrayals of foreign cultures.
body: Asked about “Argo” winning Best Picture just a year after “A Separation” won Best International Film at the Oscars, Farhadi said he watched the film at the time it came out and felt it was a “Hollywood thing.” In the film, loosely based on a true story, director Ben Affleck plays a Latino exfiltration specialist who masquerades as a Hollywood producer to rescue six Americans held captive in Tehran during the U.S. hostage crisis in Iran. The moderator mentioned how Affleck’s film portrays Iran “like you’re in hell.”

Farhadi then recalled spending time in the U.S. a few years ago when working on a project and, during research, travelling to San Francisco to speak with incarcerated men. “I met some people in prison who are Black, [some who come] from other countries, and the real America was there. But people in the world don’t see that part of the United States.”

“I have this problem when they feel they are up and they think, ‘[others] should be like us,’” he continued. “Even if it’s in a good way and they want to be kind to you, they wish ‘one day you’ll become like us,’ and no, I don’t want to.”

articles.title: Noel Gallagher guitar sells for £12,000 at auction
articles.summary: The instrument was one of a number of items which belonged to a former Oasis sound engineer.
body: A guitar which originally belonged to Noel Gallagher has been sold for £12,000 at auction.
The limited edition Epiphone instrument in Manchester City blue was one of a number of items put up for sale by the son of Huw Richards, a former front-of-house sound engineer with the band.
Another of the items in his collection, a Kangol rain jacket produced for the band's touring personnel, sold for £2,000.
But a set of unheard Oasis recordings valued at between £1.2m and £1.6m were pulled from the auction last week, after the band filed an injunction.

articles.title: Alison Hammond returns home from hospital after rushing off This Morning
articles.summary: The This Morning presenter said she believes she experienced a panic attack on Friday's show.
body: Alison Hammond has said she is home and "feeling so much better" after she went to hospital for a heart check-up after leaving ITV's This Morning midway through Friday's show.

The presenter, 51, left the programme during its live broadcast, appearing to clutch her chest as she was helped off set by co-host Dermot O'Leary. He later told viewers she was "feeling a little unwell".
Soon after Hammond said she had "a little bit of a palpitation" and was undergoing tests.
In a video on Instagram on Saturday, she said she was "all OK, all-clear, which would mean I had a massive panic attack on live TV. I mean, the shame of it."

articles.title: Behemoth! review - Pedro Pascal classical music drama hits all the wrong notes
articles.summary: New York film festival: The actor stumbles through Tony Gilroy’s forgettable film marred by stylistic gimmicks. Tony Gilroy has built a sturdy career as the director of the Bourne films and show runner of the popular Star Wars spin-off Andor.
body: As the first feature film he has directed since 2012’s The Bourne Legacy, the classical music drama Behemoth! promised to be an intriguing return from a master of threading the needle between slick action and deeply felt drama. His new film comes with a score from nine A-list composers who have banded together and called themselves The Behemoth! Collective, a stacked cast and a womanizing central character who looks phenomenal in a tux: “ Tár for straight men”, as a friend of mine put it.

If only Pedro Pascal had an iota of Cate Blanchett’s charisma or Gilroy came close to Todd Field’s elegant braiding of genres. Our protagonist is Alex (Pascal), an inscrutable cello maestro who has moved home to Los Angeles after nearly two decades on the road. The city offers him regular, if soulless, session work scoring TV shows and movies, as well as the opportunity to be closer to his brother (Will Arnett) and mother, a respected harpist who is suffering from ill health.

articles.title: Film festival celebrates British-Latino identity
articles.summary: The Latino film festival in the capital will screen 60 films from 27 countries over five days.
body: An event billed as London's only competitive Latino film festival is now under way for the first time in the capital.
Venues including the Barbican, the ICA, Ciné Lumière and BFI Stephen Street will screen 60 films from 27 countries until Tuesday.

There will also be workshops and performances with guests including Cuban dancer Carlos Acosta, a former principal at the Royal Ballet, Argentine actor Óscar Martínez, Cuban actor Jorge Perugorría and Oscar-winning Chilean screenwriter Gonzalo Maza.
The event was founded by Cuban actress Ketty Rodriguez who, when she moved to London, was struck by the lack of Latin representation in a city famous for its multiculturalism, film and history.

articles.title: Werwulf Director Robert Eggers Learned An Important Lesson From His Biggest Flop
articles.summary: Robert Eggers' The Northman may have flopped, but the Viking epic taught him a specific lesson that he applied to his latest horror film, Werwulf.
body: Robert Eggers is one of those filmmakers whose work is so well-crafted and unique that both it and his name have made a big impact on the horror genre and pop culture. This is why it's eye-opening to realize that he's only helmed four features to date. His fifth, "Werwulf," is due to hit theaters this winter, and judging by its trailers, it'll likely be another landmark horror film.

Of course, not every movie can be a hit, and Eggers has succumbed to that fate before. The dark fantasy action epic "The Northman" is his most ambitious movie yet, and thus far, it's the only one he's directed that's almost entirely removed from the horror genre. Mind you, it still features some of the gnarliest gore of his career, as well as some eerie visual elements.

articles.title: Zach Bryan Wears ‘Free Palestine’ Shirt During Concert at Robert Kraft’s Gillette Stadium
articles.summary: The performance follows Gillette Stadium owner Kraft's prior controversy with Macklemore over his removal from Ed Sheeran's tour due to his pro-Palestinian statements.
body: Zach Bryan wore a “Free Palestine “ shirt while performing at Gillette Stadium on Friday night for his With Heaven On Tour following owner Robert Kraft defending his move to urge for Macklemore ‘s removal from Ed Sheeran ‘s tour after making pro-Palestinian remarks in earlier shows.

In photos and videos captured by fans and shared on social media, Bryan can be seen wearing a black shirt with the “Free Palestine“ wording while several of his band members also wore Palestine-branded clothing.
The country singer is having a two-night run at Kraft’s stadium, slated to close his tour on Saturday night.

Bryan’s “Free Palestine” shirt comes amid controversy surrounding Kraft, owner of the New England Patriots and Gillette Stadium. Rapper Macklemore previously alleged that he was dropped from being an opener on Sheeran‘s tour after Kraft “rallied some of the other stadium owners and collectively they gave him an ultimatum: if Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues.” During his opening set at MetLife Stadium, Macklemore had publicly shouted “Free Palestine” and showed footage from Gaza on the screen behind him.
